oeeHelp.title: How OEE is calculated
oeeHelp.intro: The three factors are computed from the same queried range without rounding; OEE is their product.
oeeHelp.availability: A · Availability = run time ÷ planned time.
oeeHelp.performance: P · Performance = min(ideal time for the pieces produced ÷ run time, 1). Ideal time adds, span by span, pieces × that span standard in s/piece.
oeeHelp.quality: Q · Quality = good pieces ÷ (good + rejected pieces).
oeeHelp.unknownIdeal: Some span has no attributable standard: performance and OEE stay empty instead of being invented.
oeeHelp.rounding: Multiplying the visible percentages may differ in the last decimal because rounding happens after the calculation.
oeeHelp.units: Units: the machine cycle is measured per shot; the OEE standard is per piece = ideal cycle per shot ÷ active cavities of the run. Outside a run the machine base standard in s/piece applies.
oeeHelp.shots: A shot is not a piece: pieces = shots × active cavities of that span. Good and reject counters are already pieces and are never multiplied again.
oeeHelp.example: Example: 28 s/shot with 4 cavities = 7 s/piece; 400 pieces are worth 2,800 s of ideal time; 100 shots × 4 cavities = 400 pieces, with 10 rejected 390 are good.
oeeHelp.machineHours: Plant totals are machine-hours: eight machines in one day add up to eight days of time. Shifts bound planned time; without shifts the whole interval counts. Line stops deduct run time without doubling machine stops.
